context: An access port attaches an ordinary station to one Ethernet group. An inter-switch trunk carries several VLANs between switches.

concepts.title: Read the access port’s effective membership
concepts.text: A default access choice still assigns the port to VLAN 1 in this switch model. Clearing an explicit choice returns it to that default. A station normally sends its access port an untagged Ethernet frame.

concepts.title: Read the trunk’s native setting separately
concepts.text: The native VLAN tells a trunk how to carry untagged frames between switches. Both ends of the supplied trunk agree on VLAN 88. This setting has no effect on the desk’s default access VLAN.

concepts.title: Test the intended and unintended neighbors
concepts.text: An Ethernet connection may be up while a desk is in the wrong group. Use an Ethernet broadcast to see who can receive a frame. Check the legacy pair separately after making a change.

worked.label: Clear the bench desk’s explicit choice
worked.value: Use switch default → Effective access VLAN 1
worked.explanation: The class counter still receives Ethernet broadcasts with that desk.

worked.label: Read the floor uplink separately
worked.explanation: The two switches interpret untagged trunk frames as VLAN 88. The bench desk still uses VLAN 1.

worked.label: Move the desk to the bench workgroup
worked.explanation: The bench peer now receives the desk’s broadcast. The legacy counter and monitor still work together.

practice.title: Compare explicit and default membership
practice.action: Choose Use switch default in the New desk access VLAN row. Read the Effective access VLAN and the native setting above it.
practice.observe: The port still belongs to VLAN 1 while both trunk ends use native VLAN 88.

practice.title: Follow the intended workgroup
practice.action: Choose Bench Desk and Class Counter in Ethernet endpoints. Select Test Ethernet. Change the desk’s access VLAN to match the Bench Peer’s port and test both pairs.
practice.observe: The counter loses visibility while the bench peer receives the desk frame.

practice.title: Verify the existing legacy connection
practice.action: Select the two legacy devices in Ethernet endpoints and select Test Ethernet. Then select Check workspace.
practice.observe: The legacy connection still works after moving the desk.

requirements: Move the Shipping Desk into the same Ethernet segment as the Shipping Peer.
Keep the two legacy devices working together, separate from the Shipping Desk.
goal: Put a new desk in its workgroup while preserving the working default-VLAN devices.

review.introduction: Gives the adjacent Ethernet and IP concept before the example and compares their distinct output.
review.example: Learners use isolated switches to edit current settings and deliberately test an earlier failure.
review.assignment: Uses independent fixed topology and validates actual Ethernet reachability, requirements and bounds.

context: An Ethernet VLAN keeps local traffic in one group. A station sends traffic for another IP subnet to its default gateway. A switch can provide that gateway through a switch virtual interface (SVI).

concepts.title: Give each VLAN its own gateway
concepts.text: An SVI is a switch’s IP interface for one VLAN. Choose a usable address that is not already assigned in that VLAN’s subnet. Enable the interface. Its line state requires an active local port carrying the VLAN.

concepts.title: Check the remote switch separately
concepts.text: A local SVI can be up even when the far end of an active trunk does not admit that VLAN. Compare the far uplink’s allowed VLANs with the stations’ access memberships.

concepts.title: Check both delivery and replies
concepts.text: Enable IPv4 routing and point each station at the gateway in its own subnet. Test delivery and a reply. The gateway can pass IPv4 traffic between VLANs while Ethernet broadcasts stay within each VLAN.

worked.label: Bench gateway and default next hop
worked.explanation: Use one unused address in the bench subnet as the SVI for VLAN 32.

worked.label: Demo service gateway
worked.explanation: The server replies through its own switch virtual interface for VLAN 64.

worked.label: Forwarding and far uplink
worked.value:
IPv4 routing enabled
VLAN 32 and 64 allowed
worked.explanation: A probe returns in both directions. An Ethernet broadcast still cannot reach the other VLAN.

practice.title: Prepare the two routed interfaces
practice.action: Enter 198.51.100.1/24 in the VLAN 64 Gateway IPv4/prefix field. Enable IPv4 routing. Before editing the far uplink, scroll to Path endpoints, choose Bench A and Demo Server, then select Test IPv4.
practice.observe: The gateway interface can report Up even while the path to the demo server fails.

practice.title: Connect the far VLAN and set the reply path
practice.action: Allow VLAN 64 on the far uplink. Set 198.51.100.1 as the Demo Server’s default gateway. Set 192.0.2.1 for both bench stations.
practice.observe: The trunk admits the traffic, and all three stations have a gateway in their own subnets.

practice.title: Compare both tests
practice.action: In Path endpoints select each bench station with the demo server. Select Test IPv4 and Test Ethernet. Test Ethernet between the two benches, then select Check workspace.
practice.observe: Both IPv4 comparisons receive a reply. The demo server shares no Ethernet broadcast with the bench. The benches still share their own segment.

requirements: Enable IPv4 routing and both VLAN gateway interfaces. Use distinct usable gateway addresses with the prefixes shown.
Give each of the three stations the default gateway for its VLAN and admit both VLANs at the far uplink.
Both studio stations need an IPv4 reply from the render server. Preserve studio Ethernet delivery and keep the server’s broadcasts separate.
goal: Repair the VLAN gateways and restore IPv4 delivery and replies while keeping Ethernet traffic separated.
